messages.author: David Case
messages.body:
On Sat, Jan 04, 2020, ankita mehta wrote:
>my simulation run is stuck and my min.out is showing attached.
The default value for ntb is 1 (indicating a periodic system), but your
input coordinates are not for a periodic system.  If you didn't set up a
box in the tleap script, then you need to set ntb=0 in your &cntrl
namelist.
....dac

messages.author: David Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Jan 05, 2020, ankita mehta wrote:
>Why tleap is considering all ALANINE to be NALA?
We have so little information about what you did, and what pdb file you
loaded, to offer any useful information.  You apparently used a sequence
command, but we don't have any information about what step that was, or
what was in it.
Generally, the default in tleap is to make change an N-terminal ALA
residue to NALA.  Note that NALA (and other N-terminal residues) does
not have an "H" atom in it.  Do you have any unwanted TER cards in you
PDB file right before the ALA residues?
....dac

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
The sequence command builds a linear structure. Leap makes no attempt to
model a reasonable structure. You would need other tools for that, such as
Rosetta or Modeler.

messages.author: David Case
messages.body:
On Sun, Jan 05, 2020, ankita mehta wrote:
> what is the solution to remove TER inserted before ALA?
>It cinsiders all alanine to be NALA?
Just to repeat: we have no idea what sequence (or other commands) you
used.  It is generally far better to tell us what you actually did, not
what your intent was.  That is, don't say "I'm trying to build a pdb file
through sequence command" (that describes your intent); rather say "here
are the exact commands I gave to tleap, and here was the result." (that
describes what you actually did.)
In this particular case, as Carlos has noted, the structures Amber
creates by default are not intended to be realisitic configurations.
....dac

messages.author: Cory Ayres
messages.body:
If those are your commands, all of your alanines are NALA because you're
explicitly classifying them as such. Change NALA -> ALA in your sequence
and that should fix it.
Best,
Cory
